topic: Smart Pointers for Dynamic Memory Management
explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers are used to manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They encapsulate raw pointers and provide ownership semantics, making resource management safer and more expressive compared to manual new/delete operations. This approach leverages RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) principles, which tie resource lifetime to object lifetime.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of smart pointers—specifically std::unique_ptr and std::shared_ptr—to manage dynamic memory for a Widget object. The unique_ptr ensures exclusive ownership, automatically deleting the object when it goes out of scope. The shared_ptr allows multiple owners, with the object being destroyed only when the last shared_ptr is destroyed. This exemplifies modern C++ memory management practices that improve safety and code clarity by avoiding manual delete calls and preventing memory leaks.
